tasks.short: Find training needs, prepare lessons and cases, teach nursing staff at the bedside, sign off skills and keep records.

steps.what: Clinical nurse specialist identifies training needs from incidents, audits and new equipment
Clinical nurse specialist prepares the lesson, slides, case examples and quiz

loop.input: The current version of the hospital protocol and the learning goals set by the clinical nurse specialist.
loop.output: Three patient case scenarios and ten quiz questions with answers.
loop.check: Every question and answer must cite the protocol paragraph it tests; the clinical nurse specialist reads each answer against that paragraph's content, not only its number; no patient data from the record is used; unclear items are rewritten by hand.
loop.stop: One draft and one redraft; then the clinical nurse specialist writes the cases.
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning protocol text into realistic cases and plausible wrong answers is writing; a template cannot invent the scenario.

steps.what: Clinical nurse specialist checks the final quiz and cases before release: each answer matches the current protocol version, and it goes to the right units' e-learning
Clinical nurse specialist releases the checked quiz and cases in the learning system
Clinical nurse specialist instructs nursing staff at the bedside and in short sessions
Clinical nurse specialist observes nurses perform the skill and judges their competence
Clinical nurse specialist signs the competence sign-off

Clinical nurse specialist records attendance and sign-offs in the learning system: typed in later today; after the change sign-offs exist when signed and attendance is ticked during sessions, so only checking and corrections remain
Nurses complete the e-learning and quiz

tasks.design: Skill sign-offs are signed on a tablet in the {LMS} instead of a paper card, which takes about as long, but the record then exists the moment it is signed and no longer has to be typed in later; attendance is ticked on the same tablet during sessions, and a view shows which skills expire per unit. A bounded step drafts case scenarios and quiz questions from the current protocol version, each citing its paragraph, for the clinical nurse specialist to check and release. Bedside teaching and observing competence stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Competence cards were paper and re-typed, and writing cases took evenings.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning systems take sign-offs on mobile devices, and language models draft cases that can be checked against protocol text.
tasks.still_hard: Skills are learnt at the bedside; per-nurse competence views may need works council consent.
tasks.human_edge: Showing a nurse how it is done, watching them do it and knowing when they are ready.

ambition.what: Expiring skills refreshed before they lapse on every unit, not after an incident.

tasks.altitude: The clinical nurse specialist approves materials instead of writing them all and spends the time teaching.

reach.learn: Whether unit-level expiry views help plan skills days.

evidence.claim: Learning systems record sign-offs on mobile devices and show expiry of competences.
A system that can monitor staff performance needs works council consent.
Providers are responsible for careful use of generative AI, including training staff.

assumptions: Boundary: from training needs to sign-off recorded; the hospital-wide education programme is outside.

Input contract: incident reports and audit results from the quality team; current protocol versions from the document system; skill list per unit set by the nursing management; sign-offs and attendance captured on the tablet by the clinical nurse specialist in s5 and during sessions; fallback is paper cards.
Expiry views show units and skills; individual views go only to the nurse and their manager.
Nurses' learning time is outside the clinical nurse specialist's savings.

s2 keeps 50 for reading every drafted item against the protocol; the release check (s2b) and release (s2c) take 1 each. s6 keeps 20 for checking the records and corrections; ticking attendance during sessions takes about the time a paper list took.
unknowns: Whether the learning system supports mobile sign-off.
Number of skills signed off per year.
research_questions: Do drafted cases change quiz pass rates compared with hand-written ones?

already_counted.description: Clinical nurse specialist checks drafted cases and quiz answers against the protocol.

incremental.description: Clinical nurse specialist keeps the question bank linked to current protocol versions.
Education office maintains skill lists and the learning system.

approvals.approved_version: The quiz and case scenarios exactly as checked by the clinical nurse specialist in s2b against the current protocol version, released once to the named units' e-learning; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: teaching is mostly ad hoc at the bedside with few prepared lessons, so s2 keeps 80, and many sign-offs still go on paper, so s6 keeps 60 (9.6); high: prepared lessons and tablet sign-offs as designed (20.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Track protocol review dates, check new guidelines, revise the protocol, consult, get it approved and publish it.

steps.what: Clinical nurse specialist tracks which protocols are due for review: in a spreadsheet today; after the change reads the reminders from the protocol library
Clinical nurse specialist searches for new evidence-based practice guidelines and literature
Clinical nurse specialist compares the protocol with the guideline and drafts the revised procedures

loop.input: The current protocol, the new guideline text and the clinical nurse specialist's list of points to change.
loop.output: A tracked-changes revision with a change table: protocol paragraph, old text, new text, guideline paragraph.
loop.check: Every change must cite a guideline paragraph that supports its meaning; medication doses must equal the guideline or the current protocol and are checked against the national drug database; unchanged paragraphs must stay word for word.
loop.stop: One draft per protocol and one retry; then the clinical nurse specialist edits by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Matching guideline recommendations to local procedure text needs reading both; a document compare only shows differences in wording.

steps.what: Clinical nurse specialist consults nurses, physicians and the pharmacist on the draft
Protocol committee reviews and approves the revised protocol
Clinical nurse specialist checks the version to publish: exactly the version the committee approved, and the right units for read-confirmation
Clinical nurse specialist publishes and announces the protocol: formatted and announced by hand today; by one release in the document system with read-confirmation tasks after the change
Clinical nurse specialist answers questions and checks the protocol is followed on the ward

tasks.design: The protocol library in {DOCS} holds review dates and owners and sends reminders; saved guideline and literature alerts feed the clinical nurse specialist. A bounded step drafts a tracked-changes revision with a change table that cites the guideline for every change, and after the protocol committee approves, the clinical nurse specialist checks the version and releases it unchanged in the document system with read-confirmation tasks for the units.
tasks.previous_blocker: Review dates lived in spreadsheets and revisions were rewritten by hand, so many protocols ran past their review date.
tasks.enabler_now: Document systems manage versions and approvals, and language models can draft revisions that a change table makes checkable.
tasks.still_hard: Local practice and expert opinion fill gaps guidelines leave; drafts can misread a recommendation, and the inspectorate expects careful use of generative tools.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what works on this ward and getting colleagues to agree to change.

ambition.what: Every protocol reviewed on schedule and within weeks of a guideline change, not years later.

tasks.altitude: The clinical nurse specialist reviews drafted revisions and leads consultation; approval stays with the committee.

reach.learn: Whether the change table speeds their review of dose changes.

evidence.claim: The national drug database checks doses, interactions and contraindications, with content set by the pharmacists' association.
Protocol and literature work suits an artefact generator with citations and committee approval.
Providers are responsible for careful use of generative AI: know the risks, train, test and monitor.

assumptions: Boundary: from a review falling due to the protocol published and checked on the ward.

Input contract: protocol library with owner and review date per protocol, kept by the document controller; guideline alerts from the professional bodies' sites set up by the clinical nurse specialist; fallback is the spreadsheet and manual search.
Committee and consultee time is outside the clinical nurse specialist's savings.
Consultation and ward follow-up do not change.
s1 keeps 10 for reading reminders. s3 keeps 60 because every change in the table is read against the guideline. s6 keeps 20 for the release; the version check (s5b) takes 1 of its old share.
unknowns: How many protocols the clinical nurse specialist owns.
Share of protocols past their review date today.
research_questions: How often does the committee change a drafted revision compared with a hand-written one?

already_counted.description: Clinical nurse specialist checks each change in the change table against the guideline.

incremental.description: Clinical nurse specialist triages guideline alerts and keeps citations current.
Document controller keeps templates, owners and review dates current.

approvals.approved_version: The protocol version exactly as approved by the committee in s5 and checked by the clinical nurse specialist in s5b, published once in the protocol library with read-confirmation tasks to the named units; any later edit needs a new committee approval and check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: protocols built on local expert opinion have no guideline to draft from, so s3 keeps 90 (21.5); high: guideline-based protocols as designed (31.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose indicators, audit records, review incident themes, observe practice and report findings to management.

steps.what: Clinical nurse specialist chooses the indicators and audit questions
Clinical nurse specialist opens a sample of records and scores the audit by hand
Clinical nurse specialist reads incident reports and groups them into themes

loop.input: Free-text incident reports of the period for the unit.
loop.output: One theme per report from the hospital's fixed theme list, with the sentence that supports it.
loop.check: The theme must come from the fixed list, the quoted sentence must appear in the report, and the quoted sentence must itself state the fact the theme rests on; in the random sample and for every 'other' the clinical nurse specialist confirms that the quote supports the chosen theme; if agreement falls below the set level, all reports are read by hand.
loop.stop: One pass per report; unclear reports go to the clinical nurse specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reporters describe the same problem in many different words; keyword rules miss or mislabel them.

steps.what: Clinical nurse specialist observes practice on the ward and interviews nurses
Clinical nurse specialist evaluates the quality and effectiveness of nursing practice
Clinical nurse specialist assembles the report: indicator charts, theme tables and written findings
Clinical nurse specialist presents the findings to the nursing manager and quality committee
Nursing manager decides on improvement actions

tasks.design: Nursing quality indicators (pain scored, fall risk screened, pressure ulcer checks, documentation completeness) are computed per unit from structured record fields on the {DATA_PLATFORM}, replacing most hand-scored record audits. Incident reports are grouped into fixed themes by a bounded step with a sampled check, and the report template pulls indicator charts; observation, judgement and the conversation with management stay with the clinical nurse specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Audits meant opening records one by one, and incident themes were counted by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Governed data platforms compute indicators from record fields, and language models can classify free text when quotes and sampling check them.
tasks.still_hard: Indicators show what is recorded, not what is done; incident data is sensitive and must stay inside the hospital.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing why practice differs from the protocol and turning findings into changes nurses accept.

ambition.what: Every unit sees its nursing indicators monthly instead of after a yearly audit.

tasks.altitude: The clinical nurse specialist interprets indicators and themes instead of counting them; improvement decisions stay with the nursing manager.

reach.task: Analyse incident trends across the hospital
reach.learn: Whether the fixed theme list holds across departments.

evidence.claim: Quality indicators can be computed per unit from structured record fields on a data platform.
Providers are responsible for careful use of generative AI, including testing and monitoring.
Indicators per nurse would monitor staff performance and need works council consent; this design reports per unit.

assumptions: Boundary: from choosing indicators to improvement actions decided; carrying out the actions is outside.

Input contract: pain scores, screenings and checks recorded by nurses in the record; incident reports filed by staff in the incident system; indicator definitions agreed with the quality committee and built by the data analyst; fallback is hand audits.
Indicators are reported per unit, never per nurse.
Nursing manager time is outside the clinical nurse specialist's savings.
s2 keeps 40 for checking indicator outliers against records; s3 keeps 50 for the sampled check; s6 keeps 50 because the written findings are the clinical nurse specialist's own.
unknowns: Whether the hospital has a governed data platform with record data.
Number of incident reports per unit per quarter.
research_questions: Do computed indicators agree with hand audits on the same records?

already_counted.description: Clinical nurse specialist checks indicator outliers against a few records.
Clinical nurse specialist reviews the sample of theme assignments.

incremental.description: Clinical nurse specialist keeps indicator definitions and the theme list current.
Data analyst maintains the indicator queries.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: key items are recorded as free text, so indicators cannot be computed and hand audits remain (s2 keeps 80) (16.3); high: structured fields for most indicators (24.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take a consult request, read the record, observe, interview and examine the patient, identify care needs and advise.

steps.what: Ward nurse requests the consult with the reason and urgency
Clinical nurse specialist takes the consult request from the ward by phone
Clinical nurse specialist reads the record before seeing the patient
Clinical nurse specialist observes, interviews and examines patients at the bedside
Clinical nurse specialist talks with the ward nurse and the family
Clinical nurse specialist identifies care needs and gives advice
Clinical nurse specialist types the consult note and advice into the record

tasks.design: Wards request consults as an order in the electronic health record ({OTHER}) with a reason and urgency, so requests queue in one list instead of by phone. The consult note uses a template whose advice items become proposed care plan actions for the ward nurse to accept; observation, interviewing and judgement do not change.
tasks.previous_blocker: Consults came by phone and advice sat in notes the ward had to copy into the care plan.
tasks.enabler_now: Records support consult orders and templates that propose care plan actions as configuration.
tasks.still_hard: Assessing a complex patient is hands-on and cannot be shortened.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing what the ward has missed and giving advice that nurses can carry out tonight.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; requests and advice move through the record.

reach.task: Carry out consult advice in the care plan
reach.learn: Whether proposed actions are accepted faster than advice in notes.

evidence.claim: Records support consult orders and note templates that propose care plan actions.
The record is kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Boundary: from the consult request to the advice recorded; carrying out the advice is outside.

Input contract: consult orders with reason and urgency entered by ward nurses in s1, replacing their phone call at about the same effort; advice templates set by the clinical nurse specialists; fallback is the phone.
Ward nurse time is outside the clinical nurse specialist's savings.
Record reading, bedside assessment and advice do not change.

s7 keeps 80: the template saves layout, but the consult note and advice are the clinical nurse specialist's own first record. Saving the note is their own save; the proposed care plan actions take effect only when the ward nurse accepts them, so no approval is needed here.
unknowns: Whether consult orders exist in the record.
research_questions: Does consult advice reach the care plan faster as proposed actions?

incremental.description: Clinical nurse specialist keeps advice templates current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: wards keep phoning, so s2 keeps 90, and the template fits few consults, so s7 keeps 90 (1.6); high: consult orders and the template used as designed (5.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The clinical nurse specialist keeps teaching, assessing and leading change; protocol drafting, audits and records shift to checking.
skills_to_grow: Reviewing drafted protocol changes against guidelines
role.ambitious_version: A clinical nurse specialist whose protocols are always current and whose units see their quality monthly.
